Lamine:

Welcome to the distance sampling mailing list.  Some comments about your questions interspersed below.  In addition to what I have provided here, recognise there is a >300 page Distance Users Guide that is shipped with Distance.  You can access it via the menu under Help | Online manuals.  In the manual there are two examples of data import in Chapter 3 getting started.

On 17/06/2014 10:56, Lamine M Benrabah wrote:

I feel very uplifted to find a good support system fro Distance! as a die hard Mac user i am finding it an uphill batle with soooo many obstacles.

I finally installed windows partition and parallels JUST for this program. It is extremely complicated.

Specifically i have completed field experiments using 1km linear transects. I did not use Distance to design the survey but want to use it to analyse my data. Iam having trouble plugging my data, importing it, and analysing it.

I was unable to locate the details and explanation regarding input or perpendicular to the transect line SPECIFICALLY Left side of the transect line distances observed are they Positive integers and Right side observed distances are negative values? How doe we differentiate this? And the input of the orientation of Transects eg. N, W, E, S. Clustered animals with individual count.

Detections on either side of the transect are "folded over;"   it does not matter the side of the transect where the detection was made.  All that needs to be recorded is the perpendicular distance from the transect.  No positive or negative signs used.  Transect orientation is also irrelevant to the analysis and is not part of the data used.  If you have clusters of animals, you would record the number of individuals in the clusters in the observation layer.

I think you are on the right track with the data organisation; you will not provide units with your stratum area.  Distance (in its basic form) does not use "distance along transect" in the analysis, but it does need to know the amount of effort you exerted, so total transect length needs to be recorded.

Have a look at the video
http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/ericr/simple-Distance-data-import.mp4 for a tutorial on data import.

You could also have a look in a local library for a copy of Buckland et. al (2001) Introduction to distance sampling. Oxford Univ. Press. for descriptions of the fundamentals of distance sampling.
any help direction or referrals would be greatly appreciated.
